name: TPMO disclaimer
definition: The agent gives the third-party marketer disclaimer: in substance, "we do not offer every plan available in your area."
action: Script: read it in the opener, before any benefit (today's rule; from October 2022 to September 2026 it was the first minute). Real time: a prompt as a safety net if a benefit comes up first. After the call: send calls without it to QA.

notes.v2: Negated variants ("don't offer every plan", "not able to offer every plan") and the State Health Insurance Program.
notes.v3: Adds "not contracted with every carrier". Keeps the Medicare.gov and 1-800-MEDICARE wording, though no call in this set used it.

name: Recording notice
definition: The agent, or a recorded message, says the call is recorded or monitored.
action: Play the notice automatically when the call connects. After the call: flag calls with no notice before the handoff, since several states require consent from everyone on the call.

notes.v2: "This call is recorded or monitored", "for quality and training", "recorded line".
notes.v3: Simpler: any "recorded", "monitored", or "for quality and training".

name: Medicare affiliation claim
definition: The agent says or clearly implies they are calling from or for Medicare or the government, or that Medicare itself is updating the customer's benefits.
action: Same-day QA alert, then coach the agent on approved openers. Implying a call comes from Medicare is a misleading-marketing risk.

notes.v1: One phrase: "calling from Medicare". It caught nothing, because agents rarely say it outright.
notes.v2: "Your Medicare is getting updated or upgraded", "calling on behalf of Medicare", "Medicare is updating".
notes.v3: Allows words in between ("your Medicare benefits are getting upgraded") and excludes "I'm not from Medicare".

name: Money-back claim
definition: The agent promises money added to the customer's Social Security check, or a giveback or premium reduction paid back to them.
action: Compliance check: before the transfer, confirm a Part B giveback plan really exists in the customer's area. Promising money that isn't available is a top complaint driver.

notes.v1: One phrase: "social security". It fires on any mention.
notes.v2: "Money back", "give back", "on your Social Security check", "Part B reduction".

name: Do-not-call request
definition: The customer asks not to be called again, to be taken off the list, or to stop calling.
action: Compliance: stop the pitch, add the number to the internal do-not-call list, and alert if the pitch continues after the request.

notes.v2: Seven phrasings ("take me off your list", "stop calling") and six exclusions for the agent's own "I'll put you on the list".

name: Not interested
definition: The customer explicitly declines the offer, for example "I'm not interested" or "no, I don't want it".
action: Real time: one approved rebuttal, then a polite close if the customer declines again.

notes.v2: Six phrasings and eight exclusions ("if you're not interested").
notes.v3: Trimmed to the phrasings that held up.

name: Already covered
definition: The customer says they already have coverage or a plan they want to keep, such as a supplement, Medicaid, the VA, a union or an employer plan.
action: Real time: suggest asking what they like about their plan and comparing benefits, rather than pushing a switch.

notes.v2: "I have a supplement", "I'm happy with my plan", "through my union or employer".
notes.v3: Adds a question-and-answer clause: a "yes" right after "do you have Medicaid or a supplement?" counts.
notes.v4: Adds "I have [carrier]", "I have Medicaid, the VA or a supplement", and utterance matching.

name: Trust concern
definition: The customer questions the call's legitimacy or their privacy: suspects a scam, asks how the caller got their number, or refuses to give information over the phone.
action: Real time: suggest the agent offer verification (company name, license number, a callback number) before asking for anything personal.

notes.v2: Scam or fraud, "how did you get my number", refusing to give information on the phone.
notes.v3: More scam words and privacy refusals.
notes.v4: Adds "giving information over the phone", "why do I need the card", and utterance matching.

name: Transfer to licensed agent
definition: The agent transfers the call, or clearly sets up a live transfer, to a licensed agent, specialist or enrollment team, and the customer goes along with it.
action: Outcome metric: this is the conversion event for these calls. Track it by script, time of day and lead source.

notes.v2: "Transfer or connect you to", "stay on the line", only after the first 20 seconds.

name: Medicare number request
definition: The agent asks the customer for their Medicare card number, Medicare ID or MBI.
action: Compliance: watch for numbers collected before a licensed agent is on the line, especially right after a trust concern.

notes.v2: MBI or ID, "the number on your card", "read me the number", the red, white and blue card.
notes.v3: Excludes "I'm not asking" and "I don't want to give".
notes.v4: Drops the card check, which is now its own moment, and excludes the licensed agent asking later and Social Security numbers.

name: Can't hear or understand
definition: Someone says they can't hear or understand the other person, or asks for something to be repeated.
action: Coaching: high rates point to line quality or pace. Suggest the agent slow down and confirm.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: Card not handy
definition: The customer says their Medicare card isn't with them, or that they have to go find it.
action: Real time: offer to hold or book a callback instead of losing the transfer.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: Unsure of own coverage
definition: The customer says they don't know what plan or coverage they have, or that a family member handles it.
action: Real time: suggest reading the card together, or inviting the family member who manages it.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: Asks what the call is about
definition: The customer asks what the call is about or why they are being called.
action: Script: the opener isn't stating its purpose clearly. Test a clearer first line.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: Bad time, call back
definition: The customer says it's a bad time (busy, driving, at work) or asks to be called back later.
action: Real time: offer a specific callback time and log it.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: Too many calls
definition: The customer complains about getting too many of these calls.
action: Insight: a sign the list is saturated. Feed it into lead-source scoring and call-frequency caps.

notes.d1: Drafted from the theme review of 100 development calls.

name: "No one will call you again"
definition: The agent promises the customer will stop getting these calls, often as a reason to finish the call.
action: Compliance: an agent can't promise calls will stop. Send to QA, especially after a do-not-call request.

notes.d1: Found while reading do-not-call calls: agents answered genuine requests with "complete this call and no one will call you".

name: Card-ready check
definition: The agent checks whether the customer has their Medicare card with them, usually just before a transfer.
action: Funnel step: measure drop-off between this check and the transfer.

notes.d1: Split out of the Medicare-number rule after its false alarms turned out to be this step.
